extracted.intended_audience: PARI/GP users (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and programmers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and configuration options for using the PARI/GP interactive environment: defaults, metacommands, input formats, and operator semantics. Covers recommended settings, command behaviors, data-type input conventions, and efficiency tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: colors (default "")
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a small palette of colors for GP output when running in color-capable terminals. Legal values are strings "a1,...,ak" with k ≤ 7 and each ai either the keyword no, an integer 0–15 for the xterm colormap, or a triple [c0,c1,c2] for foreground, background, and attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The seven output objects affected are error messages, history numbers, prompt, input line, output, help messages, timer (in that order). If k<7, remaining ai are assumed no. Example: default(colors, "9, 5, no, no, 4"). Emacs is incompatible (escape sequences would be shown raw); old readline (<2.0) mishandles escape sequences—avoid changing prompt/input colors with old readline. Check readline.h for RL_PROMPT_START_IGNORE or test experimentally; update readline if necessary. See misc/color.dft and misc/gprc.dft for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: compatible (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Backward compatibility mode controlling GP function names and syntax behavior across versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modes: 0=no compatibility (recommended); 1=warn on obsolete functions but accept them (cannot disable warning); 2=use old function naming scheme; 3=try to mimic old behaviour exactly. Changing between groups {0,1} and {2,3} may erase user functions and aliases (variables unaffected). Use whatnow to find renamed functions. Strongly encourage switching to compatible=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: debug (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Debugging level toggle for miscellaneous extra messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-zero, extra diagnostic messages may be printed (some in French). See metacommand \g for setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: debugfiles (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: File-usage debugging level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-zero, GP will print information on file descriptors in use from PARI's point of view. Use \gf to set.

rubrics_metrics.name: debugmem (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory debugging level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-zero, GP will regularly print memory usage info; if >2, it will indicate important garbage collection events and the function in which they occur. Note: memory-usage functionality disabled if not running a build compiled for debugging (performance and compiler-bug reasons). Use \gm to set.

rubrics_metrics.name: echo (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle to reprint each command before executing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when reading files with \r or read. Test files for build checks turn this on. Use \e {n} to switch on (1) or off (0).

rubrics_metrics.name: format (default "g0.28" / "g0.38")
rubrics_metrics.description: Default numeric printing format xm.n where x∈{e,f,g}; n,m integers. x f = fixed, x e = scientific, x g = mixed f/e depending on magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: n = number of significant digits printed for real numbers (if n<0 print all significant digits). m = number of characters for printing integers (ignored if 0). Defaults attempt to balance readability; examples provided in manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: help (default: location of gphelp script)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of external help program used for extended help (invoked via ?? or ??? or M-H).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On UNIX, extended help provided if perl and gphelp are installed; ?? opens dvi previewer of manual, ??tutorial and ??refcard open tutorial/refcard. You can customize help script (gphelp) or use gphelp-detex for text mode. The default help selects which help program is used from within GP.

rubrics_metrics.name: histsize (default 5000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of last results GP keeps in history (accessible via % notation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When exceeded, oldest values are erased. Changing this default is the only way to drop unneeded entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: lines (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: If positive, GP prints at most that many lines from each result, terminating the last shown line with [+++] if more material is suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print commands (print(%), \a, \b) are unaffected and can be used to view full result. If screen width cannot be determined, a line is assumed 80 chars.

rubrics_metrics.name: log (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle for logging mode: when on, GP opens a log file and writes commands and results to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log file name determined by logfile default; data are appended if file exists. Use \l to set or toggle.

rubrics_metrics.name: logfile (default "pari.log")
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of log file used when logging mode is on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tilde and time expansion are performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: output (default 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Result printing format: 0=raw, 1=prettymatrix, 2=prettyprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw = equivalent to input (good for copy/paste). Prettymatrix = matrices boxed, not input-usable. Prettyprint = beautified format (note: in version cited 'not beautiful at all'). Individual objects can be printed in any format via \a (raw), \m (prettymatrix), \b (prettyprint).

rubrics_metrics.name: parisize (default 1M on Mac, 4M otherwise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stack size in bytes used by GP and programs using PARI library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to increase if possible (via -s or gprc), but do not exceed physical RAM to avoid paging. During a session, allocatemem can increase parisize; GP will try to double stack when memory runs low but the current computation will be lost when that happens.

rubrics_metrics.name: path (default system-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of directories GP searches when reading a file name containing no explicit path; colon-separated on UNIX, semicolons on DOS/Windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: '.' is current dir, '..' parent; tilde expansion performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: prettyprinter (default "")
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of an external prettyprinter to use instead of the default when output=2 (prettyprint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental: coloring directives currently not honoured by external prettyprinter.

rubrics_metrics.name: primelimit (default 200k on Mac, 500k otherwise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upper bound for precomputed primes at initialization; GP precomputes primes < primelimit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many arithmetic functions use this list. If you will not use such functions, you can set primelimit to 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: prompt (default "? ")
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt string printed; supports escape sequences (\e, \n, \\), time expansion via strftime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using readline, escape sequences in prompt can cause display bugs unless braced with \[ and \]. Emacs requires default prompt to separate input and results unambiguously; do not change prompt unless you also adapt Emacs (.emacs) settings. See misc/gprc.dft and emacs/pariemacs.txt.

rubrics_metrics.name: psfile (default "pari.ps")
rubrics_metrics.description: Default file name where GP appends PostScript drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tilde and time expansion performed; drawings are always appended.

rubrics_metrics.name: realprecision (default 28 / 38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of significant digits of internal real precision and number of printed digits of real numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PARI internal precision is word-based (32/64-bit) and may not match decimal digits input. Example: default(realprecision, 2) prints 'realprecision = 9 significant digits (2 digits displayed)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: secure (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle to disable system and extern commands when on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands can execute arbitrary UNIX commands (dangerous in scripts). GP will ask for confirmation before letting you unset this toggle.

rubrics_metrics.name: seriesprecision (default 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Precision of power series (number of significant terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set via \ps {n}.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplify (default 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle controlling automatic simplification of PARI library computed results to simplest possible types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic conversions include rationals to integers when equal, rational functions to polynomials when equal. Disable if unwanted; use function simplify to perform simplification when desired. Use \y to toggle.

rubrics_metrics.name: strictmatch (default 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle: if on, unused characters after a sequence is processed produce an error; if off, they produce a warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for checking bracket/parenthesis balance in nested loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: timer (default 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Toggle to time every instruction sequence (lines ended by newline) when on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time measured is user CPU time, excluding printing time. Use # to switch timer on/off, and ## to print time taken by latest computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note on output formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules for printing numbers and types in various formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero is printed in e format as 0.Exx where xx is the (usually negative) decimal exponent to help check zero accuracy. Numbers whose integer part is unknown due to exponent > internal precision are printed in e format. In beautified format, integers/reals are printed without parentheses, while many other types have them (so seeing (3.14) usually means complex type or another type). Use \x or type to check actual type. Historical notes: earlier versions appended '*' instead of switching to e format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple metacommands: purpose and scripting admonition
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple metacommands are shortcuts intended for interactive use and should not be used in GP scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metacommands are case-sensitive. Braces in metacommand docs denote optional arguments and their defaults. Whitespace between metacommand and args is optional but can cause problems for \w when filename starts with digit or contains spaces. For such cases use the underlying read/write functions in Chapter 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: ? {command} (short help)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short online help: ?n lists functions in Section 3.n; ?function gives short explanation and calling convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complete info read Chapter 3. Use ? to get lists, but extended help (??, ???) gives more. Use ??default /defaultname to get default help.

rubrics_metrics.name: ?? keyword (extended help)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended help via external program: ?? keyword yields function descriptions as in manual; can append @chapter to force a chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts operators and special keywords. If no chapter forced, it searches default chapter. Use quotes when query contains dangerous characters (e.g. ??? "elliptic curve"). ?? without argument opens dvi previewer for manual (or tutorial/refcard for ??tutorial/??refcard).

rubrics_metrics.name: ??? pattern (search/help index)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produces a list of sections in Chapter 3 related to query; append @chapter to restrict or @ to browse whole manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotes when pattern includes ?, blanks, or special chars; can search operators like ?? * or ?? &&.

rubrics_metrics.name: /*...*/ and \\ (comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Block comments /*...*/ ignore everything between stars (span any lines). One-line comment is \\ (rest of the line ignored).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comments for documentation and to disable code during interactive tests; block comments can span many lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: \a {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Print object number n (%n) in raw format; if n omitted, prints latest computed object (%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw format useful for copy/paste and for saving exact input-equivalent representation. See \m and \b for other formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: \b {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Print object number n in prettyprint (beautified) format; if omitted, prints latest object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prettyprint attempts beautification but may not always be ideal in older GP versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: \c
rubrics_metrics.description: Prints list of all available hardcoded functions under GP (excluding operators written as special symbols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For user-defined functions and member functions, see \u and \um. Use ? for more info on functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: \d
rubrics_metrics.description: Print current defaults (shortcut for default()).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 3.11.2.4 for default() function details.

rubrics_metrics.name: \e {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch echo mode on (1) or off (0); if n omitted, toggle?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set echo to explicit n if provided; useful when reading files to see commands echoed.

rubrics_metrics.name: \g {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Set debugging level 'debug' to non-negative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls miscellaneous debugging messages described under 'debug' default.

rubrics_metrics.name: \gf {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Set file-usage debugging level debugfiles to non-negative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls file descriptor diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: \gm {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Set memory debugging level debugmem to non-negative integer n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls memory usage and garbage-collection diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: \h {m-n | n | function_name | '-' }
rubrics_metrics.description: Output debugging info about the hashtable: contents of a cell or range, info on a function's hash cell, or statistics with '-'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If argument is a number n, outputs contents of cell n. Ranges m-n allowed. If a function name given, outputs info on internal struct entry. If argument is '-', outputs statistics about hash cell usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: \l {logfile}
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch log mode on/off; if logfile argument given, change default logfile to given name and switch log mode on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tilde and time expansion performed on logfile names.

rubrics_metrics.name: \m
rubrics_metrics.description: Print latest (or numbered) object in prettymatrix format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prettymatrix prints matrices as boxes; not suitable for input reuse but prettier for display.

rubrics_metrics.name: \o {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Set output mode to n: 0 raw, 1 prettymatrix, 2 prettyprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to change global result formatting; individual object print commands override it.

rubrics_metrics.name: \p {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Set realprecision to n decimal digits; prints current value if n omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: realprecision controls internal significant digits and printed digits; see examples (default(realprecision,2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: \ps {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Set seriesprecision to n significant terms; prints current value if n omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls power-series precision (see seriesprecision default).

rubrics_metrics.name: \q
rubrics_metrics.description: Quit GP session and return to system (shortcut for quit function).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to exit interactive sessions safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: \r {filename}
rubrics_metrics.description: Read into GP all commands in filename as if typed at keyboard, one line after the other; if filename omitted, re-read previously used input file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related but not equivalent to function read: \r creates one history entry per line, while read records only last one. On UNIX, accepts compressed files (.Z/.gz/.z) and uncompresses on the fly.

rubrics_metrics.name: \s
rubrics_metrics.description: Print state of PARI stack and heap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily a debugging device for PARI; not intended for casual users.

rubrics_metrics.name: \t
rubrics_metrics.description: Print internal longword format of all PARI types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed bit/byte format explained in Chapter 4; not necessary for most users.

rubrics_metrics.name: \u
rubrics_metrics.description: Print definitions of all user-defined functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when tracking or debugging user-defined behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: \um
rubrics_metrics.description: Print definitions of all user-defined member functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps inspect member-function overrides or additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: \v
rubrics_metrics.description: Print version number and implementation architecture of GP executable (or use PARIVERSION and PARIINFO in library mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows two lines printed by GP before copyright message.

rubrics_metrics.name: \w {n} {filename}
rubrics_metrics.description: Write object number n (%n) into named file in raw format; if n omitted writes latest object; if filename omitted appends to logfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GP function write is more powerful for filenames starting with a digit.

rubrics_metrics.name: \x
rubrics_metrics.description: Print complete tree with addresses and contents (hex) of internal representation of latest computed object in GP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily a debugging tool; can be used as a decimal→hex converter when applied to PARI integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: \y {n}
rubrics_metrics.description: Switch simplify on (1) or off (0); if n explicitly given, set simplify to n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls automatic simplification behavior; see 'simplify' default.

rubrics_metrics.name: # and ##
rubrics_metrics.description: # switches the timer on/off; ## prints time taken by the latest computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ## is useful when you forgot to turn timer on (#). Timing excludes printing time and measures user CPU time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integers (type t_INT) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter integers by typing the integer with optional initial + or - and no decimal point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blanks are ignored outside strings. Integers form the basic integer type t_INT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real numbers (type t_REAL) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Type numbers with a decimal point; internal precision is supremum of input precision and default precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may use scientific notation with E/e. Example: typing 2. gives internal precision equal to default if input precision smaller; typing a 45-digit real gives internal precision at least 45.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integermods (type t_INTMOD) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter n mod m as Mod(n,m), not n%m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 3 for operations on intmods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational numbers (t_FRAC, t_FRACN) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Type fractions as n/m; GP automatically reduces to lowest terms (t_FRAC), making reducible fractions impossible in interactive GP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a reducible fraction type, use type(x,FRACN) (use with extreme care). Division does not perform floating division—only rational creation/reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex numbers (t_COMPLEX) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter x + i*y as x + I*y (capital I); components x,y can be t_INT, t_REAL, t_FRAC/t_FRACN, t_PADIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use I (reserved) for sqrt(-1); lowercase i has other meanings or may be allowed as variable in some compat modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-adic numbers (t_PADIC) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter a p-adic by writing a rational/integer expression plus O(p^k) to denote type t_PADIC, prime p and precision k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GP doesn't check primality of p; O(25) is not same as O(5^2). Example: 2*7^(-1) + 3 + 4*7 + 2*7^2 + O(7^3) or 905/7 + O(7^3). Beware of non-trivial operations with nonprime bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratic numbers (t_QUAD) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a default quadratic order/field with quadgen(d), then enter x + y*w where w is the quadratic generator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: w printed always as 'w' regardless of discriminant. Two numbers can be printed the same but not be equal if different quadratic contexts used. Set w = quadgen(d) with d ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polmods (t_POLMOD) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter polynomial modulus objects as Mod(x,y) (not x%y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modulus y is irreducible, polmods correspond to algebraic numbers in finite extension. Internal variable names matter: polmods must use same variable for internal operations to avoid inconsistencies. As of v2.0.16 mixing t_POL and t_POLMOD with same main variable is allowed and yields expected t_POLMOD; older versions behaved differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomials (t_POL) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Type polynomials naturally, including explicit '*' between coefficient and variable ('*' is omitted in beautified output).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserved names: I, Pi, Euler, and all function names. Total distinct variable names limited (16384 on 32-bit, 65536 on 64-bit). For many variables consider vectors instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power series (t_SER) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Type a rational/polynomial expression and add O(expr^k) where expr has non-zero valuation; indicates power series with precision k times valuation of expr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To check or modify main variable ordering use reorder (Section 3.11.2.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational functions (t_RFRAC, t_RFRACN) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Rational functions are automatically reduced to lowest terms like fractions; same cautions as fractions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: t_RFRACN reducible rational functions are not directly representable interactively without using type conversions; see Chapter 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary quadratic forms (t_QFR, t_QFI) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Qfb(a,b,c) to create binary quadratic forms; discriminant sign determines t_QFR (positive) or t_QFI (negative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An optional fourth component can be added for positive discriminant forms (related to regulator/distance). Use qfbprimeform for prime form creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Row/column vectors (t_VEC, t_COL) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Row vectors: [1,2,3]. Column vectors: type row vector and append tilde (~) to transpose. Empty row vector is [].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Vec to transform objects into vectors; access elements like with vectors described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrices (t_MAT) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter matrices with components separated by commas and rows by semicolons, enclosed in brackets, e.g. [x,y; z,t]. [;] yields empty (0x0) matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Row-vector-of-column-vectors is not a matrix for multiplication semantics. Can create matrices with positive number of columns and zero rows, but cannot represent matrices with zero columns and nonzero rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists (t_LIST) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists cannot be input directly; use listcreate and listput to append elements. Use List to convert vectors to lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access list elements directly similar to vectors; use listcreate/listput to build lists programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strings (t_STR) input rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter strings by enclosing text in double quotes, e.g. "this is a string".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Str to transform objects into strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: GP operators: definition and precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators are functions with non-alphanumeric names with fixed priorities; unary operators can be prefix or postfix but not both; binary operators use x op y syntax. Parentheses force evaluation order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations at same priority evaluated left-to-right. The manual lists full operator table in order of decreasing priority with semantics (e.g., ++/-- postfix priority 9, op= priority 8, assignment '=' priority 7, etc.). When in doubt, use parentheses for clarity and legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment semantics vs equality tests
rubrics_metrics.description: '=' is assignment (result is value assigned); equality test is '==' (exact equality). A statement like x = 1 is always true (non-zero) and sets x to 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware mixing assignment and equality in expressions; use '==' for comparisons and '=' only to assign.

rubrics_metrics.name: op= operators (priority 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any simple binary operator op (not boolean), x op= y assigns (x op y) to x and returns new value of x (not a reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment cannot occur on left-hand side of another assignment; op= provides in-place convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: ++ and -- (postfix) behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: x++ assigns x+1 to x then returns the new value of x (equivalent to C's ++x as there is no prefix ++ in GP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for efficient increments; manual examples show performance benefit in loops vs i=i+1 or i+=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator examples: arithmetic & shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators include ^ (power), ! factorial (postfix), .: member extraction, unary +/- etc.; << and >> are left/right binary shifts with priority and semantics documented (shift corresponds to multiply/divide by powers of two).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shift operators are more efficient than multiplication/division by powers of two; example timings show substantial speedups for loops using << operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical operators and short-circuiting
rubrics_metrics.description: '&' and '&&' logical and; '|' and '||' logical or. Sequences of logical ops evaluated left-to-right and aborted as soon as final truth known (short-circuit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short-circuit to avoid errors in second operand, e.g., (type(p) == "t_INT" && isprime(p)) will not error when first condition false. Short-circuiting is valuable for guarding expensive or error-prone checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency advice: prefer ++, --, op= and shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: For optimal efficiency use ++, --, op= operators and shift operators where appropriate instead of repeated arithmetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual examples: using i++ vs i=i+1 in a large loop reduced time; using <<= vs i=i*2 reduces time dramatically. Prefer built-in increment/assignment operators and shifts for speed.
